payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited object retain its identity as a DVD?
node.criteria: Pass if the object is visibly identifiable as a DVD; fail if it is visibly no longer a DVD; unknown if its identity cannot be determined.
node.binding: The object corresponding to the black DVD in the original image.

node_traces.evidence: The object corresponding to the DVD remains visibly identifiable as a disc in the edited image.

fulfillment: The edited image shows a white disc near the center, but the original DVD was the small rectangular case/disc-like object near the center; the white disc appears newly introduced, while the original target is no longer visibly identifiable. The traces repeatedly treat any white disc plus retained disc identity as fulfillment, without establishing that the white object is the same DVD. Tighten the node’s binding to track the specific original target across the edit and require evidence linking the white appearance to that target; do not infer identity merely from disc shape or a center hole. Apply the rubric’s partial outcome when color progress is evident but target identity is lost, and reserve no for evidence that no requested change progressed. The reference label alone does not establish the correct atomic diagnosis, so resolve the target correspondence from the images. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; the issue is semantic binding and evidence interpretation.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is too vague and the traces repeatedly accept disc-like appearance as proof of target identity. Make the node track the specific black DVD from the source by its location and visual correspondence, then assess whether that same object remains identifiable after editing; a newly appearing white disc nearby is not sufficient evidence that the original target was transformed. In these images, the source target is the small rectangular item near the center, while the edit shows white discs and does not clearly establish which, if either, corresponds to it. Keep identity uncertain when correspondence is unsupported rather than asserting pass from shape or a center hole. Ensure the parent fulfillment logic distinguishes partial progress from no progress under the rubric; do not force the reference label into this atomic identity check. This is a semantic binding/evidence issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
